newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC expected to agree on regulatory cooperation.
newsitem.headline: APEC expected to agree on regulatory cooperation.

text.p: Finance ministers of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum are expected to endorse initiatives on regulatory cooperation at a meeting here this weekend, host the Philippines said on Friday.

"A set of voluntary principles is expected to be endorsed" by APEC's top financial officials, including initiatives on international regulatory cooperation, said a Philippine government statement announcing the opening of the meeting.

Among them were: "Anti-money laundering efforts; enhanced cooperation among export credit agencies; strengthening clearing and settlement systems; (and) ratings support for capital market development."

The meeting agenda includes current macroeconomic issues and policies to support free flow of capital, facilitating private sector participation in infrastructure development, and promoting financial and capital market development.
The ministers will consider recommendations in several of these areas from an advisory group of APEC member leading financiers, the statement also said.
It did not elaborate, but a working paper from the group obtained by Reuters suggested it would recommend as a priority developing a framework for cross-listing of securities among members.
"This would be a great leap forward in terms of cross-border financing," the document said.
It also urged development of bond markets in emerging member economies which would "greatly increase liquidity for infrastructure projects" to be funded in local currencies.
Another recommendation was for better and more transparent economic data, with multilateral agencies and developed economies helping provide the necessary expertise.

The 18-member APEC forum comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and the United Sates.
